title: Op-ed | Drying Up? The Future of the UK’s Diplomatic Pipeline
content:
As the UK faces growing international challenges and proposed cuts to the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), questions are being raised about the future of British diplomacy and the next generation of diplomatic talent. Drawing on his experience working with the OSCE Mission in Kosovo and serving as one of the UK’s Youth Delegates to the G20 in 2026, Alastair Nicol explores the barriers facing young British people seeking careers in diplomacy and the opportunities for the UK to invest in its future diplomatic workforce.

In 2025, I spent six months with the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe’s (OSCE) Mission in Kosovo. For an internationally-minded young person looking to gain experience in a field operation, Kosovo is a rich environment. 27 years after the Kosovo War (1998-99), the country  continues to host NATO’s Kosovo Force (KFOR), the United Nations, the European Union, the OSCE, and an array of diplomatic missions.
